area: determinism: the in-process gate has a structural blind spot; cross-process check added

find.report_claim: the README documents `--verify-determinism --frames 1800` as the canonical regression shield, and game.snapshot() feeds the hash it compares
find.live_evidence: keystone/testing.py verify_determinism runs `factory()` twice INSIDE ONE PROCESS, so both passes share a PYTHONHASHSEED and any ordering derived from set or dict-of-strings iteration is identical in both; the gate therefore cannot detect hash-seed-dependent nondeterminism
find.consumer_evidence: injecting `self.weapon = next(iter({"pulse", "scatter", "lance", "surge"}))` left `--verify-determinism` reporting ok:true, while separate processes produced 3bf71e94 vs 03b51121 -- so a replay recorded in one session would not reproduce in the next, and the canonical gate said everything was fine

read: shooter/sim.py snapshot (a progress record, not a full state hash)
killed: treating the snapshot's omitted fields (spawn_t, RNG state, player velocity, enemy cooldowns) as a bug: keystone's GameModule contract only requires snapshot() to return a dict, and nothing claims it is an exhaustive state record -- calling that a defect would repeat cycle 165's error
changing keystone's verify_determinism to fork processes: another worker owns that tree and it would slow every engine user's gate
claiming the snapshot is the problem: the omission matters only if it hides divergence, and the cross-process test shows the real risk was the gate's structure, not the payload
analyze.survivor: run the same simulation in separate processes with different PYTHONHASHSEED values and assert one hash, which is what a player replaying a saved transcript actually does

fix.shooter: tests/test_cross_process_determinism.py (3 tests) runs `play.py --simulate --frames 120` under PYTHONHASHSEED 0/1/424242 and asserts a single hash, checks a fixed game seed is reproducible while a different seed differs (via the playtest runner, since --seed belongs to it), and replays bot_campaign.json in a fresh process with PYTHONHASHSEED 31337 asserting it still wins at wave 4

shooter.baseline: the shipped game is cross-process deterministic today: seeds 0, 1 and 12345 all produce 7e4b602e029d12d68672790318d119cd over 120 frames
shooter.mutation: injecting a hash-seed-dependent starting weapon left the in-process gate green but failed BOTH the cross-seed test (3bf71e94 / 03b51121 / 770aaa8b) and the replay test; shooter/sim.py was restored byte-identically (sha256 match).
